title: Derived global cohomology of finite-field constructible complexes is insensitive to the two algebraic-closure coefficient topologies
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology. On profinite sets with finite jointly surjective covers put $C(P)=\{f\in C(P,\Omega): f(P)\subset F\text{ for some finite }\mathbf Q_\ell\subset F\subset\Omega\}$ and $B(P)=C(P,\Omega)$ [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed, def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Write $c:C\to B$ for inclusion, $C_X=p_X^*C$, $B_X=p_X^*B$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Fix a finite intermediate field $E\subset\Omega$, with the restricted norm topology, and put $A=p_X^*\underline E$ [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. All module categories are internal module categories, with their ordinary unbounded derived categories [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] and derived relative tensor and internal Hom [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Bounded constructible below means the finite constant local model convention [sk-def-sfb-constructible].

For every bounded constructible $V\in D(A)$ let
$$m_V:\operatorname{Res}_{A\to C_X}(C_X\otimes_A^L V)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Res}_{A\to B_X}(B_X\otimes_A^L V)$$
be the actual morphism in $D(A)$ induced by $c_X$, represented on a flat-term K-flat resolution $P$ by $z\otimes v\mapsto c_X(z)\otimes v$ [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars]. On forgetting coefficient actions and applying derived global sections on the small pro-etale site [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology], the morphism
$$R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{proet}},m_V):R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{proet}},C_X\otimes_A^L V)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{proet}},B_X\otimes_A^L V)$$
is an isomorphism in the ordinary derived category of abelian groups. This asserts neither that $m_V$ is a sheaf-level isomorphism nor that derived internal Hom commutes with $A\to B_X$. No flatness of $c_X$, completeness of $\Omega$, or finite global cohomological dimension of $k$ is assumed.

proof.text: Choose a separable closure k^s/k and its profinite Galois group G. Apply the geometric finite scalar model to V. This gives the equivariant object K_A=mathcal K_A(V), bounded with cohomology underline W_q for finite-dimensional continuous E-representations W_q, together with the actual projection isomorphisms beta_C and beta_B. Their coefficient square identifies the geometric image of m_V with the scalar-inclusion map C tensor_A^L K_A -> B tensor_A^L K_A. All hypotheses hold: X is separated finite type, ell is invertible in k, and V is bounded constructible with the required finite constant local models.

proof.text: Use the exact functors F_C,F_B and their shift-compatible natural transformation alpha from the profinite representation comparison. For every q, its heart assertion applies to W_q and says alpha_(H^q(K_A)[0]) is an isomorphism. Its exact shift compatibility gives the same assertion on H^q(K_A)[-q]. No claim of finite cohomological dimension is made here: these objects and their derived invariants remain in the ordinary unbounded target category.

source.place: Paragraph (3), agent reduction of the coefficient-topology obligation; exact norm-topology literature input WANTED.

proof.text: If K_A=0 the assertion is immediate. Otherwise choose integers a<=b containing its cohomological support. The standard truncation triangles give a finite tower whose successive factors are H^q(K_A)[-q], for a<=q<=b: truncate at q and shift the standard truncation triangle by q; the quotient has only its q-th cohomology and hence is that heart object shifted by -q. Apply triangle two-out-of-three to the exact functors F_C,F_B and alpha at each of these finitely many triangles, starting with the zero truncation below a. The factors were treated in the preceding step. Induction proves alpha_(K_A) is an isomorphism. Only the boundedness of K_A is used, not convergence of an infinite Postnikov tower.

proof.text: Apply ordinary condensed Galois descent separately to C_X tensor_A^L V and B_X tensor_A^L V. By its naturality for the coefficient morphism c and the morphism C_X tensor_A^L V -> Res_c(B_X tensor_A^L V) representing m_V, R Gamma(X,m_V) is conjugate by the two descent isomorphisms to ev_* of the composite of R Gamma_G(kappa) with the canonical invariant morphism after scalar restriction. The square Res_c(beta_B) o gamma = kappa o beta_C of step 1 holds in D(A_G(C)); applying ev_* R Gamma_G and the naturality of the scalar-restriction invariant morphism in its argument (here beta_B) identifies that composite, up to the invertible ev_* R Gamma_G(beta_C) and ev_* R Gamma_G(beta_B), with alpha_(K_A), which is defined from gamma by the same scalar restriction and invariant inclusion. Step 3 makes alpha_(K_A) invertible; composition with the invertible sides proves exactly the asserted isomorphism for the actual map m_V. This uses no sheaf-level identification of C and B.
